title: Counteracting User Attention Bias in Music Streaming Recommendation via Reward Modification

problem.claim: Automatically played songs can generate false-positive user-feedback labels when users do not pay attention, introducing attention bias into recommendation-model training.

gap.claim: Existing approaches either use auto-feedback directly or heuristically delete potential false-positive labels, and both can produce biased results because the labels shift the training-data distribution.

contributions.claim: A learning-based counterfactual approach, NDB, adjusts user auto-feedback and learns recommendation models with a Neural Dueling Bandit algorithm.
NDB uses a user attention network to compute importance weights for modifying original rewards and a second neural network trained with dueling bandit for online recommendation.
The modified rewards are analyzed as statistically unbiased, and the learned bandit policy is associated with a sub-linear regret bound.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that theoretical analysis showed the modified rewards are statistically unbiased and that the learned bandit policy enjoys a sub-linear regret bound.
The authors report that NDB significantly outperformed state-of-the-art baselines in experiments.

narrative_sequence.summary: Music applications continuously recommend songs in users' daily lives.
Automatic playback can create false-positive feedback labels when users are inattentive, biasing recommendation-model training.
Existing approaches directly use auto-feedback or heuristically remove potential false positives, with biased outcomes.
The paper proposes NDB, which modifies auto-feedback using attention-derived importance weights and learns recommendations with a dueling-bandit network.
The authors report unbiased modified rewards, a sub-linear regret bound, and performance exceeding state-of-the-art baselines.

source_observation.claim: Automatic interaction signals may include false positives when users are not attending to recommended content.

interpretation.claim: Observed feedback should be adjusted for the possibility that exposure or playback does not imply meaningful user engagement.

application.claim: Use attention-aware or counterfactual reward adjustment before training recommendation policies in continuously autoplayed settings.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this approach applies unchanged to other domains, feedback mechanisms, or attention measurements.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, evaluation metrics, baseline identities, or effect sizes.
The abstract does not describe how user attention is measured or how the importance weights are estimated.
The abstract does not provide the assumptions or proof details behind the unbiasedness and regret claims.
